title: US-001: Shared RAM Buffer Registry
description:
As a plugin instance, I want access to a global shared buffer registry (`R1-R4`) so that Record and Play plugins can exchange audio by channel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Global registry exposes exactly 4 addressable buffers (`R1-R4`).
- [ ] Record and Play instances can read/write the same underlying channel buffer.
- [ ] Concurrent access is thread-safe and real-time safe (no blocking in audio thread).
- [ ] Unit tests verify write/read correctness across instances for each channel.

title: Prevent concurrent writers to same RAM buffer
description: When one Record instance is already recording to a shared RAM buffer (R1-R4), a second Record instance can start recording to that same buffer. The second start clears the buffer and both instances can then write concurrently, causing nondeterministic/interleaved results based on host processing order.
acceptance_criteria:
- Starting recording on channel Ri while another instance is already recording channel Ri is deterministic and safe (single-writer semantics).
- Existing recording on Ri is not silently clobbered by another instance's NoteOn.
- Behavior is explicitly defined (ignore second trigger, steal with explicit policy, or reject with state flag) and covered by tests.
- Cross-instance tests verify no concurrent-write race on the same channel.
- cargo fmt --check passes.
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.
- cargo test passes.
close_reason: Implemented generation counters for per-channel recording ownership. When a new instance starts recording on a channel, it bumps the generation; the previous writer detects the mismatch and stops. Most-recent-write-wins policy with deterministic single-writer semantics.

title: Calibrate sampler character against Machinedrum UW captures
description: Current model uses signed 12-bit round/clamp, linear interpolation, stepped 12-to-2-bit BRR, sample-and-hold SRR and tanh drive. These are approximations. Acquire gain-staged real UW recordings of transient drums, swept tones and quiet decays at unity and octave shifts; compare spectra, quantization error, clipping and pitch images against identical Ultrawave renders. Verify BRR/SRR mappings and fixed sample-clock behavior at 44.1/48/96 kHz. Do not promote Octatrack evidence in technical_specs.md to Machinedrum facts. Add measured fixtures and tolerances before claiming fidelity. Jeff can measure his own unit when home. First record its revision/OS, routing and gain settings, disable effects, and capture an interface loopback baseline without normalization. Separately measure known-sample playback, external-input RAM capture and internal MLEV resampling; use sweeps, stepped-level tones and quiet decays, then pitched transients. Align latency/clock drift before comparison, keep interface coloration distinct, and preserve held-out drum loops for level-matched listening. Model repeatable magnitude/phase response only if measured; EQ alone cannot reproduce nonlinear quantization, clipping or pitch-dependent aliases. Match the MD response rather than flattening it, and do not bake assumed ADC/DAC coloration into each internal resampling pass. Elektron OS1.63 manual p71 specifies 12-bit sample playback; p86 specifies 44.1kHz 24-bit A/D and D/A converters; A15-A16 distinguishes MLEV internal rerouting and ILEV external input. It does not establish the exact internal RAM rate, interpolation, filter curve or master tap. Source: https://www.elektron.se/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/machinedrum_manual_OS1.63.pdf. Retrigger follow-up: measure all RTIM 1-127 intervals at multiple tempos, including values below 32, and verify envelope restart/live-control semantics. uwretrig now implements official OFF/infinite/tempo-relative behavior using Legofriendly's reported landmarks at https://tarekith.com/assets/machinedrum_tipsandtricks.htm#Reference, logarithmic interpolation between them and doubling-per-32 extrapolation below 32. That curve is not firmware-derived or hardware-verified; replace approximations only with measured fixtures.

title: Correct retrigger timing, disabled interval and infinite-count semantics
description: Investigation found four correctness gaps. Official Elektron OS1.63 manual A15 specifies RTRG127 infinite and RTIM tempo-relative, with RTIM0 disabling RTRG; A16 says RAM Play matches ROM25-48. Current RamPlay uses finite counts including 127, linear 0-500ms intervals independent of host tempo, and increments the counter before rendering the initial sample. Reproduced through actual CLI with a one-frame 0.5 impulse at 44100Hz: RTRG2/RTIM127 emits frames [0,22049,44099], not [0,22050,44100] for its advertised 500ms; RTRG3/RTIM0 emits [0,1,2] instead of just [0]; RTRG127/RTIM1 emits 128 pulses then stops at frame21970 despite a 0.75s render. Ordinary retriggers after sample end and reverse restarts work. Existing four retrig-filtered tests pass: the basic test checks only stored count and the reverse test preserves the legacy early first repeat. Add independently derived impulse-timeline tests, exact count/off/infinite boundaries, forward/reverse and short-sample gaps, block partition/MIDI offset invariance, stop/reset/new-note and buffer invalidation, plus host tempo handling. Verify the exact RTIM value-to-beat mapping from authoritative evidence or hardware before claiming MD timing accuracy; also verify envelope and live automation semantics. Keep real-time safety and saved parameter IDs; define compatibility implications of changing timing units. Source: https://www.elektron.se/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/machinedrum_manual_OS1.63.pdf. No DSP behavior changed during this investigation.
close_reason: Corrected OFF, infinite count, first-repeat timing and tempo-relative scheduling with fractional-frame carry and phase-preserving tempo changes. New notes replace trains; OFF cancels pending hits; stop/reset/source replacement cancel trains including silent gaps. Count/time latch on note except OFF; NoteOff does not choke. Saved IDs/raw values remain compatible but old RTIM patches sound different. 93 workspace and 9 wrapper tests pass debug/release, fmt, Clippy, six offline renders, VST3 strictness5 and both CLAP validators (18 passed/3 unsupported skipped each). Exact CLI and callback tests cover tempo, fractional intervals, MIDI offsets/block sizes and reverse; allocation test covers infinite reverse and tempo changes. Renoise 3.5.4 at 48kHz passes every tapered-tone frame at 60/120 BPM, 256 infinite hits and RTIM OFF, plus reverse, routing, One Shot, immediate save/reopen and volatile RAM. Pattern ZT commands avoid callback-time BPM restoration; duration assertions verify host tempo. Both editors and OFF/INF/musical/beat labels visually inspected. Warm fast loop 4s. RTIM uses community landmarks with disclosed interpolation/extrapolation; hardware curve/envelope/automation calibration remains open in uwab.
